props.title: Millcreek buildings and canopy cover zones (2023 lidar), planning estimate
props.snippet: Building footprints with lidar roof heights, and tree canopy cover by ownership zone, for Millcreek, Utah, from 2023 lidar. Unvalidated planning estimate; not surveyed or field-verified.
props.accessInformation: City of Millcreek GIS. Lidar: 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS 3DEP, project UT_2023SaltLakeCo_C24). Building footprints: Salt Lake County Assessor and Surveyor (downloaded October 19, 2026). Parcels: City of Millcreek parcel layer (2025 tax year).
props.description:
Planning estimate. This layer is an unvalidated estimate derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. It has not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use it for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

What it shows

Two layers for Millcreek, Utah:

  • Buildings (22,042 polygons): Salt Lake County's building footprints inside or crossing the city limits, each with roof-height statistics measured from the 2023 lidar. 21,562 footprints have a height; 480 have no lidar roof inside them and their height fields are empty (possible reasons include buildings demolished since the County drew them, very small structures and roofs hidden under trees).
  • Canopy cover zones (13 polygons): the share of the ground covered by tree canopy at least 2 m tall, for the whole city and for groups of land by ownership (private, public and its owner groups, uncertain owner, and land outside every parcel). Citywide canopy cover is 25.59% of the observed area (2,103 acres).

Typical uses: a citywide look at building heights and massing, finding tall or unusual buildings for review, canopy goals and comparisons between ownership groups. Heights are roof minus ground, not building heights as a building code defines them.

How it was made

  • Roofs. Every lidar point was classified three independent ways: this project's own first classification, the IGN FRACTAL model, and Esri's pretrained building model. A point counts as roof when at least two of the three call it building. The roof surface is the highest first or single return in each 0.5 m cell from those points.
  • Ground. The bare-earth terrain is interpolated at 0.5 m from the ground-classified returns (under a building it is interpolated from the ground around it).
  • Heights. For every 0.5 m cell whose centre lies inside a footprint (and inside the city), roof elevation minus terrain elevation. A footprint's median (HEIGHT_P50_M), 95th percentile and maximum are taken over the cells that have both a roof and terrain value. Footprint shapes and County attributes are unchanged.
  • Canopy. A canopy height model at 0.5 m: vegetation returns minus terrain, with roofs masked out. Canopy is any observed cell at least 2 m above the ground. Cover for a zone is canopy cells as a share of the zone's observed cells, counted by cell centres.
  • Zones. From the City's parcel layer: parcels grouped by owner with fixed rules (named public agencies, schools, housing authorities and districts are public; everyone else, including utilities, churches and nonprofits, is private; missing or mixed owners are uncertain), dissolved by group and clipped to the city. "No parcel" is the city outside every parcel, mostly streets and other rights-of-way. Zones overlap: the whole-city zone contains all the others and the public owner groups sit inside "Public / government parcels", so do not add areas across rows.

Accuracy and checks

  • Roof classification, against 1,217 hand-labelled roof and non-roof parts on one 1 km tile (a deliberately hard sample, not a citywide accuracy): 92.8% of roofs found; 2.8% of non-roof parts called roof.
  • Vegetation classification, same tile: 95.9% of tree parts called vegetation; 10.7% of non-vegetation parts called vegetation; shrubs 76.5%.
  • Roof support. 2,380 footprints have a lidar roof on less than 80% of their area (LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT). Their heights are less reliable: lower roofs, porches and carports are often the part missed. Of the footprints with at least 95% support, the 3D blocks built from these heights are within 1 m of the median roof for all but 13 of 14,229.
  • Canopy coverage. About 99.4% of every zone is observed by the lidar; the low and high bounds in the layer show how far the unobserved cells could move each figure (about half a point at most).
  • Copies. Every value and every footprint shape was checked against the source library before upload (0 rows differ), and the projection to Web Mercator was checked vertex by vertex (all within 0.07 mm of Esri's own projection with the ITRF08 transformation).
  • None of these figures is a field validation. No building height has been compared with a survey or a plan set.

Limits

  • Heights are roof-minus-terrain estimates, not code-defined building heights (which are measured to a defined point of the roof from a defined grade). Chimneys, rooftop equipment, parapets and branches over a roof raise the maximum; the median is the safest single figure.
  • Footprints are the County's. A footprint can hold several buildings, a building can have several footprints, and buildings built or demolished since the County drew them show up as missing or empty roofs. 22,042 is a count of footprint records, not of buildings.
  • Many County fields are empty in this snapshot (BLDGHEIGHT, SOURCE, most ADDRESS and BuiltYear values). They are carried unchanged so the layer joins back to the County's.
  • Canopy at 2 m includes tall shrubs and excludes lower plants. Leaf-off trees in early November may be under-counted where few returns came back from bare branches.
  • Do not use Shape__Area or Shape__Length for measurement. ArcGIS Online computes them in Web Mercator, which inflates areas here by about 1.74 times and lengths by about 1.32 times. Use FOOTPRINT_M2 and ZONE_ACRES, which were computed in UTM before upload.

Coordinates and heights. Built in NAD83(2011) / UTM zone 12N (EPSG 6341), metres, and taken to WGS84 / Web Mercator for ArcGIS Online with the transformation WGS_1984_(ITRF08)_To_NAD_1983_2011. Every layer in the Millcreek LiDAR 2023 set uses this same transformation, so the layers line up with each other and with Esri's basemaps to a few centimetres; without it they would sit about 1.2 m apart. Elevations are NAVD88 (Geoid18) in metres; heights are metres above the lidar bare-earth terrain.

Lidar source. The 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS project UT_2023SaltLakeCo_C24, USGS 3D Elevation Program), flown on October 7, November 2 and November 4, 2023. Quality level 1 means at least 8 pulses per square metre and a vertical accuracy (RMSEz) of 10 cm or better on open, non-vegetated ground under the USGS specification; the vendor's own accuracy report for this project has not been reviewed for these products. The points were reclassified for these products (see "How it was made"); the products are gridded at 0.5 m.

FOOTPRINT_M2 Footprint area (m2) Double square metres True ground area of the whole footprint polygon, computed in NAD83(2011) / UTM 12N before upload (0.10 to 19,324.6 m2). Use this for area, not Shape__Area. Multiply by 10.7639 for square feet.
AOI_PCT AOI_PCT Double percent Share of the footprint's area inside the Millcreek city limits, 0 to 100. Under 100 for the 27 footprints that cross the boundary (PARTIAL_AOI = 1); their statistics use only the part inside.
ROOF_COV_PCT Roof support (% of footprint cells) Double percent Roof support: ROOF_CELLS as a percentage of GRID_CELLS, 0 to 100. The share of the footprint's 0.5 m cells that have a lidar roof (2 of 3 classifiers agree) and terrain. Under 80 sets LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT. A review indicator, not an accuracy. Empty for the 3 footprints with no cell centre.
ROOF_Z50_M Median roof elevation (m, NAVD88) Double metres, NAVD88 (Geoid18) Median elevation of the lidar roof cells in the footprint, in metres above the NAVD88 datum (Geoid18), 1,297.6 to 1,764.2. Empty for the 480 footprints with no roof cell.
GROUND_Z50_M Median ground elevation (m, NAVD88) Double metres, NAVD88 (Geoid18) Median bare-earth terrain elevation in the same cells as the roof statistics, in metres NAVD88 (Geoid18), 1,294.4 to 1,757.9. Under a building the terrain is interpolated from the ground around it. Empty for the 480 footprints with no roof cell.
HEIGHT_P50_M Median roof height (m) Double metres Main height estimate: the median of roof elevation minus terrain over the footprint's cells with both values, in metres (0.80 to 37.06). Roof minus ground, not a code-defined building height. Empty for the 480 footprints with no roof cell. Feet: HEIGHT_P50_FT.
HEIGHT_P95_M 95th percentile roof height (m) Double metres 95th percentile of roof minus terrain over the same cells, in metres (0.80 to 42.22): close to the highest roof parts but not set by one stray cell. Empty for the 480 footprints with no roof cell. Feet: HEIGHT_P95_FT.
HEIGHT_MAX_M Maximum roof height (m) Double metres Highest single cell of roof minus terrain, in metres (0.80 to 43.32). Can be a chimney, antenna, rooftop unit, overhanging branch or noise; use with care. Empty for the 480 footprints with no roof cell.
GRID_CELLS GRID_CELLS Integer cells of 0.25 m2 Number of 0.5 m grid cells (0.25 m2 each) whose centres fall inside the part of the footprint within the city (0 to 77,312). 0 means a sliver with no cell centre (NO_CELL_CENTERS).
ROOF_CELLS ROOF_CELLS Integer cells of 0.25 m2 Number of those cells with both a lidar roof value and a terrain value; the cells the height statistics use (0 to 68,926). 0 means no roof support (NO_ROOF_SUPPORT).
NEG_H_CELLS Cells with roof below terrain Integer cells of 0.25 m2 Number of cells whose roof is below the terrain (negative height), 0 to 9. They are kept in the statistics; any sets NEGATIVE_HEIGHT (35 footprints).
PARTIAL_AOI PARTIAL_AOI Integer 1 if the footprint extends outside the Millcreek city limits (27 footprints), otherwise 0. Statistics use only the part inside the city.
HEIGHT_STATUS Height flags String (160) Review flags, separated by semicolons. Always UNVALIDATED, plus any of: LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT (roof on under 80% of cells, 2,380), NO_ROOF_SUPPORT (no roof cell, 477), NEGATIVE_HEIGHT (35), PARTIAL_AOI (crosses city limit, 27), GEOMETRY_REPAIRED (5), NO_CELL_CENTERS (3). Example: UNVALIDATED;LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT.
HEIGHT_P50_FT Median roof height (ft) Double feet HEIGHT_P50_M in feet (multiplied by 3.280839895, rounded to 0.01 ft; 2.64 to 121.60). Empty where HEIGHT_P50_M is empty. Roof minus ground, not a code-defined building height.
HEIGHT_P95_FT 95th percentile roof height (ft) Double feet HEIGHT_P95_M in feet (multiplied by 3.280839895, rounded to 0.01 ft; 2.64 to 138.52). Empty where HEIGHT_P95_M is empty.
Shape__Area Shape__Area Double Web Mercator square metres Polygon area computed by ArcGIS Online in Web Mercator. Not a true area: about 1.74 times too large at Millcreek's latitude. Use FOOTPRINT_M2.
Shape__Length Shape__Length Double Web Mercator metres Perimeter computed by ArcGIS Online in Web Mercator. Not a true length: about 1.32 times too long at Millcreek's latitude.

HEIGHT_STATUS flags

Every footprint carries UNVALIDATED; the other flags are added, separated by semicolons, when they apply (for example UNVALIDATED;LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT).

Flag Footprints Meaning
UNVALIDATED 22,042 Every record: no height has been checked against a survey.
LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT 2,380 Lidar roof on less than 80% of the footprint's cells (ROOF_COV_PCT under 80). A review flag, not an accuracy threshold.
NO_ROOF_SUPPORT 477 No cell in the footprint has a lidar roof; height fields are empty. Often a demolished, very small or tree-covered building.
NEGATIVE_HEIGHT 35 At least one cell has its roof below the terrain (NEG_H_CELLS above 0). Those cells are kept; no footprint has a negative median.
PARTIAL_AOI 27 The footprint crosses the city limit; statistics use only the part inside (AOI_PCT under 100).
GEOMETRY_REPAIRED 5 The County polygon was invalid and was repaired (area change under 0.000000001 m2).
NO_CELL_CENTERS 3 A sliver inside the city that holds no 0.5 m cell centre; no statistics.

CANOPY_ACRES Canopy (acres) Double acres Area of canopy at least 2 m tall in the zone: canopy cells times 0.25 m2, in acres, rounded to 0.1 acre (city 2,103.1). Counts observed canopy only.
CANOPY_PCT_OCT19 Canopy cover, October 19 (%) Double percent The same measure from the October 19, 2026 canopy, built from an earlier single classification of the same lidar. The Millcreek LiDAR 2023 set. Eight layers from the same lidar and the same processing: buildings and canopy cover zones (feature layer), 3D buildings (scene layer), bare-earth terrain (elevation layer), hillshade (tile layer), slope classes, 2 m contours, treetops and tree crowns (vector tile layers). They share one coordinate transformation and one terrain, so they can be stacked in one map or scene.

Questions or corrections: City of Millcreek GIS. The processing records (scripts, checks and run logs) are kept by City of Millcreek GIS.

These data are unvalidated planning estimates produced by City of Millcreek GIS from 2023 lidar. They are not surveyed, engineered or field-verified, and must not be used to determine property boundaries or ownership, building or site design, engineering, flood or drainage design, code compliance (including building height), or any legal or regulatory determination. They are provided as is, without warranty of accuracy, completeness or fitness for any purpose; check conditions on the ground before relying on them. Credit "City of Millcreek GIS; 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS 3DEP)" when you use or show them.

Salt Lake County data. The building footprints and their County attributes come from Salt Lake County (Assessor and Surveyor). The County's own terms apply to them: the County states that its footprints are not field verified, are for general reference only, and are not intended to determine property ownership, final building and site design or jurisdictional boundaries, or to replace a certified topographical or boundary survey or any other legal document.

Parcels. Ownership groups come from the City of Millcreek parcel layer (2025 tax-year snapshot, read October 8, 2026). A tax year is not an ownership effective date, and the grouping of owners into private, public and uncertain is the City's own rule set for this analysis, not a legal finding of ownership.

props.title: Millcreek slope classes 0.5 m (2023 lidar), planning estimate
props.snippet: Ground slope in six classes (under 10% to 30% and over) for Millcreek, Utah, from the 0.5 m bare-earth terrain of the 2023 lidar. Unvalidated planning estimate; not surveyed or field-verified.
props.accessInformation: City of Millcreek GIS. Lidar: 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS 3DEP, project UT_2023SaltLakeCo_C24).
props.description:
Planning estimate. This layer is an unvalidated estimate derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. It has not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use it for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

What it shows

The steepness of the bare ground across Millcreek, Utah, in six classes of percent slope, mapped at 0.5 m from the 2023 lidar. It answers questions such as "where is the ground steeper than 30%?" for hillside planning, and shows far more detail than slope layers made from 1 m to 10 m elevation models: street edges, embankments, retaining walls and channels appear as well as the east-bench hillsides.

Percent slope is rise over run times 100: 10% is a 1 m rise in 10 m (about 5.7 degrees); 30% is about 16.7 degrees; 100% is 45 degrees.

Legend

Each polygon belongs to one class. A break value belongs to the class above it (exactly 10.0% is "10% to 15%").

Class Percent slope Area (ha) Share of city Polygons
Under 10% below 10 2,389.3 71.42% 8,581
10% to 15% 10 to under 15 209.5 6.26% 35,783
15% to 20% 15 to under 20 113.6 3.40% 31,053
20% to 25% 20 to under 25 72.4 2.16% 25,764
25% to 30% 25 to under 30 51.4 1.54% 20,408
30% and over 30 and above 509.1 15.22% 7,763

Share of the city at or above each threshold: 10%: 28.58%; 15%: 22.32%; 20%: 18.92%; 25%: 16.75%; 30%: 15.22%.

The legend labels come from the layer's style (one style layer per class). This is a vector tile layer: it draws only. The tiles carry no attributes, so there are no pop-ups, no identify and no filtering by class. Classes can be switched on and off, or recoloured, in the style.

How it was made

  1. Slope in percent from the 0.5 m bare-earth terrain with ArcGIS Pro's Surface Parameters over a 3 m neighbourhood, computed on the whole lidar mosaic and then clipped to the city, so cells at the city limit use their full neighbourhood.
  2. Each cell put into one of the six classes.
  3. Cleanup (4 m2 minimum mapping unit). Classified as it is, the 0.5 m slope makes 924,458 patches, most under 4 m2, because on a graded hillside slope wanders back and forth across a class break. Every patch smaller than 16 cells (4 m2) was merged into its largest neighbouring patch; nothing else changed. Polygon edges follow the 0.5 m cells; there is no smoothing.
  4. Converted to 129,352 polygons and packaged as vector tiles (levels 0 to 17; clients draw deeper by overzooming).

Accuracy and checks

  • The polygons' areas equal the cleaned class raster's cells exactly for every class, and together they cover the whole city (33,453,372 m2).
  • The cleanup moves the area at or above each threshold by at most 0.54 points of city area, but it shrinks the narrow middle classes (25% to 30% loses 15% of its area to its neighbours) and removes real steep features smaller than 4 m2, such as curb faces and short walls. For exact class areas, use the uncleaned version, available from City of Millcreek GIS.
  • Tiles fetched from the hosted layer are byte for byte the package's; the tile vertices sit a median 6 cm from the source polygons (half a tile unit), against 0.7 m if the datum transformation had been left out.
  • The slope itself has not been checked against field measurements. Its accuracy follows the terrain's: QL1 lidar is specified to 10 cm vertically on open ground, and errors are larger under dense vegetation and buildings, where the ground is interpolated.

Limits

  • Slope over 3 m measures the local ground surface, including man-made edges. Expect much more "30% and over" along streets, driveways and embankments than on slope maps from coarser elevation models.
  • Under buildings the terrain is interpolated, so slope there is not meaningful.
  • Not a geotechnical or hazard assessment. Slope alone says nothing about soil, stability or ordinance status.

Coordinates and heights. Built in NAD83(2011) / UTM zone 12N (EPSG 6341), metres, and taken to WGS84 / Web Mercator for ArcGIS Online with the transformation WGS_1984_(ITRF08)_To_NAD_1983_2011. Every layer in the Millcreek LiDAR 2023 set uses this same transformation, so the layers line up with each other and with Esri's basemaps to a few centimetres; without it they would sit about 1.2 m apart. Elevations are NAVD88 (Geoid18) in metres; heights are metres above the lidar bare-earth terrain.

Lidar source. The 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS project UT_2023SaltLakeCo_C24, USGS 3D Elevation Program), flown on October 7, November 2 and November 4, 2023. Quality level 1 means at least 8 pulses per square metre and a vertical accuracy (RMSEz) of 10 cm or better on open, non-vegetated ground under the USGS specification; the vendor's own accuracy report for this project has not been reviewed for these products. The points were reclassified for these products (see "How it was made"); the products are gridded at 0.5 m.

The Millcreek LiDAR 2023 set. Eight layers from the same lidar and the same processing: buildings and canopy cover zones (feature layer), 3D buildings (scene layer), bare-earth terrain (elevation layer), hillshade (tile layer), slope classes, 2 m contours, treetops and tree crowns (vector tile layers). They share one coordinate transformation and one terrain, so they can be stacked in one map or scene.

props.title: Millcreek treetops (2023 lidar), planning estimate
props.snippet: 527,140 treetops at least 2 m tall detected in the 2023 lidar for Millcreek, Utah, by height class. Detections, not a tree census. Unvalidated planning estimate; not surveyed or field-verified.
props.accessInformation: City of Millcreek GIS. Lidar: 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS 3DEP, project UT_2023SaltLakeCo_C24).

What it shows

The tops of trees across Millcreek, Utah, as found in the 2023 lidar: 527,140 local high points of the canopy at least 2 m above the ground, each drawn as a dot coloured by its height. They give a citywide picture of where trees are and how tall they are. They are detections, not a count of trees: a broad tree can have several tops and a tree under a taller one can be missed.

Legend

Shown from 1:18,056 (zoom level 14) inward. Height is the canopy height at the treetop, in metres above the ground. Each class includes its upper value (a 5.0 m treetop is in "2 to 5 m").

5 to 10 m over 5 to 10 m 16 to 33 ft 190,326 36.1%
10 to 15 m over 10 to 15 m 33 to 49 ft 83,369 15.8%
15 to 20 m over 15 to 20 m 49 to 66 ft 29,563 5.6%
20 m and over over 20 m (tallest 42.9 m) over 66 ft 5,968 1.1%

The legend labels come from the layer's style (one style layer per class). This is a vector tile layer: it draws only. The tiles carry no attributes, so there are no pop-ups, no identify and no filtering; a treetop's exact height, ID and parcel ownership are kept by City of Millcreek GIS.

How it was made

  1. Canopy height model. Every lidar point was classified: this project's own classification refined with the IGN FRACTAL model, with buildings decided by a 2-of-3 vote that adds Esri's building model. The canopy height model is the vegetation surface minus the bare-earth terrain at 0.5 m, with building roofs excluded.
  2. Treetops. Local maxima of the canopy height model (smoothed by one cell), searched in a window that grows with height: 1 m radius for canopy 2 to 6 m, 1.5 m for 6 to 12 m, 2 m for 12 to 20 m and 2.5 m above 20 m. Peaks under 2 m and outside the city limits were dropped.

Accuracy and checks

  • On one hand-labelled 1 km tile (a deliberately hard sample, not a citywide accuracy), 95.9% of tree parts were classified as vegetation and 10.7% of non-vegetation parts were wrongly called vegetation.

  • No treetop has been checked against a field inventory, so the detection rate (trees found) and the false-detection rate are not known.

  • Lidar sees the top of the canopy. Small trees under larger ones, and trees under 2 m, are under-counted; broad or multi-stemmed trees can show several tops.
  • Some detections are not trees: structures, poles, wires and roof edges can make peaks (see SUSPECT above).

props.snippet: 400,063 estimated tree crown areas around lidar treetops for Millcreek, Utah, by treetop height class. Estimated canopy regions, not surveyed crowns. Unvalidated planning estimate; not surveyed or field-verified.

What it shows

The canopy of Millcreek, Utah, divided into estimated crowns: for each lidar treetop, the patch of canopy at least 2 m tall that belongs to it. 400,063 crowns of at least 3 m2 cover 826.4 ha (median crown 12.25 m2, about 4 m across). 15 to 20 m over 15 to 20 m 49 to 66 ft 30,404 154.4

  1. Seeds. Every treetop of the Millcreek treetops layer (527,140), plus peaks just outside the city, which only stop city crowns from spreading past the boundary.
  2. Growing crowns. A priority flood over the canopy at least 2 m tall (smoothed by one cell): each canopy cell goes to the treetop it reaches along the path that stays highest, so crowns divide along the low saddles between trees.

props.description:
Planning estimate. This layer is an unvalidated estimate derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. It has not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use it for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

What it shows

The shape of the bare ground across Millcreek, Utah, lit as if by a sun in the north-west, with buildings and trees removed. It is a detailed background for other layers: streets, channels, terraces, embankments and the east-bench foothills stand out at 0.5 m. It is transparent outside the city limits, so it sits over any basemap.

Legend

Grey levels from dark (ground facing away from the light) to light (ground facing it). The grey values are for display only: they are not elevations or slopes and should not be measured or classified. For elevation use the Millcreek bare-earth terrain layer; for slope use the Millcreek slope classes layer.

Useful from about 1:2,311,162 (zoom level 8) inward; the finest level is 18 (about 0.45 m per pixel on the ground). It works well under other layers with a multiply blend or partial transparency.

How it was made

  1. The 0.5 m bare-earth terrain, interpolated from the lidar's ground returns.
  2. Hillshade with the sun at 315 degrees (north-west) and 45 degrees above the horizon, without cast shadows, computed on the whole lidar mosaic and clipped to the city.
  3. Packaged as 256-pixel PNG tiles with transparency, zoom levels 0 to 18, on the ArcGIS Online tiling scheme. The brightest values (253 and 254, on 0.18% of cells) were lowered to 252 because the tiling tool treats 253 as transparent.

Accuracy and checks

  • At level 18, 2,752 tiles hold the city and all are present; no transparent pixel appears inside the city.
  • Sampled tile pixels match the source hillshade to a median of 1 grey level (95th percentile 3), when read in the right position; read 1.2 m off (no datum transformation) they would differ by a median of 3 and up to 107 levels.
  • Tiles fetched from the hosted layer are byte for byte the package's.
  • The terrain under it has not been checked against field survey (QL1 lidar is specified to 10 cm vertically on open ground).

Limits

  • Under buildings the ground is interpolated, so building sites look smoother than they are.
  • At zoom levels 10 to 12 a thin sliver at the city edge is not drawn; at levels 0 to 4 the city is under two pixels across.

props.description:
Planning estimate. This layer is an unvalidated estimate derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. It has not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use it for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

What it shows

Every Salt Lake County building footprint in Millcreek, Utah, that has a lidar roof, as a simple 3D block (CityGML level of detail 1.2): the footprint's outline, from the ground to a flat top at the building's median roof height. 21,561 buildings. They show the city's massing in a web scene: building heights, the scale of streets and how buildings sit on the terrain. Roof shapes are not modelled.

Each block carries its footprint's County attributes and lidar roof-height statistics (see the data dictionary), so a pop-up can show its height. The same statistics, for all 22,042 footprints, are in the Millcreek buildings and canopy cover zones feature layer; the two join on SOURCE_OID.

Using it in a scene

Put the Millcreek bare-earth terrain elevation layer in the scene's Ground, above World Elevation. The blocks were built on that terrain, so they stand on it exactly. On Esri's World Elevation alone they can float or sink by up to about a metre (see Coordinates).

How it was made

  1. Heights. For each County footprint, the median of lidar roof elevation minus bare-earth terrain over its 0.5 m cells (roof where at least two of three independent classifications agree that a point is building). The same figures as HEIGHT_P50_M in the feature layer.
  2. Blocks. ArcGIS Pro's Extract LOD2 Buildings tool at LOD1.2, from a 0.5 m surface that is the lidar roof inside the roofs and the terrain elsewhere, with the County footprints. Each block runs from the ground around the footprint to the median roof. 21,562 footprints with a height went in; one sliver of 0.5 m2 (FP_ID 21952) gave no block.
  3. Packaged as a scene layer package in WGS84 and published.

Accuracy and checks

  • Of 14,229 footprints with lidar roof on at least 95% of their area, the block top is within 1 m of the median roof for all but 13. Of the 2,380 with less than 80% roof (LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT in HEIGHT_STATUS), 695 are more than 1 m off, mostly low. 718 blocks in all are more than 1 m from the median roof (TOP_MINUS_ROOF50).
  • Block bases sit a median 0.11 m below the lowest terrain under the footprint. Four sit 3.6 to 7.2 m above it (FP_ID 22003, 16604, 4881, 6917): fully roofed sites where the tool read the ground near roof level.
  • The hosted layer's own statistics give 21,561 buildings with FP_ID 1 to 22,042, exactly the source's.
  • Roof classification on one hand-labelled 1 km tile (a hard sample, not a citywide accuracy): 92.8% of roof parts found, 2.8% of non-roof parts called roof. No block height has been compared with a survey or plan set.

Limits

  • Heights are roof-minus-terrain estimates, not code-defined building heights. Pitched roofs are shown flat at their median height, so ridges are higher than the block and eaves lower.
  • One block per County footprint. Footprints that hold several buildings, or buildings split across footprints, are shown as the County drew them; buildings missing from the County layer or built since are absent.
  • Low-support footprints (LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT) often have a lower roof part missed by the lidar classification, so their blocks are too low or too high over part of the footprint.

Coordinates

Horizontal: WGS84, taken from NAD83(2011) with the transformation WGS_1984_(ITRF08)_To_NAD_1983_2011, the same as every layer in the Millcreek LiDAR 2023 set. Vertical: the layer is labelled EGM96 (EPSG 5773), but its heights are NAVD88 (Geoid18) metres, left as they were measured. The packaging tool assigned the label because the source carried no vertical system. In the Salt Lake Valley the two surfaces differ by well under a metre, so on Esri's World Elevation the blocks sit within about that of the ground; on the Millcreek bare-earth terrain they match exactly. Block elevations run from 1,294.1 m to 1,764.2 m.

The points were reclassified for these products (see "How it was made"); the products are gridded at 0.5 m.

Field names are shown as stored (the scene layer has no aliases). Fields from SOURCE_ID to BuiltYear and GlobalID to Editor are Salt Lake County's, carried unchanged; FOOTPRINT_M2 to HEIGHT_STATUS are the lidar statistics (identical to the feature layer); FP_ID onward were added when the blocks were built. TOP_Z TOP_Z Double metres, NAVD88 (Geoid18) Elevation of the block's flat top, its highest point (1,295.55 to 1,764.18).
TERRAIN_MIN_Z TERRAIN_MIN_Z Double metres, NAVD88 (Geoid18) Lowest bare-earth terrain cell under the footprint (1,294.30 to 1,750.51).
TOP_MINUS_ROOF50 TOP_MINUS_ROOF50 Double metres TOP_Z minus ROOF_Z50_M: how far the block top is from the median lidar roof (median -0.05; -29.75 to +0.10). Large negatives are low-support footprints.
BASE_MINUS_TMIN BASE_MINUS_TMIN Double metres BASE_Z minus TERRAIN_MIN_Z: the block base against the lowest terrain under it (median -0.11; -10.91 to +7.17). Negative only hides wall below ground; four blocks are 3.6 to 7.2 m above.

HEIGHT_STATUS flags

Every block carries UNVALIDATED, plus any of: LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT (lidar roof on under 80% of the footprint's cells; a review flag, not an accuracy threshold), NEGATIVE_HEIGHT (at least one cell with roof below terrain, kept), PARTIAL_AOI (the footprint crosses the city limit; statistics use the part inside) and GEOMETRY_REPAIRED (the County polygon was invalid and was repaired). Property Value
Units Metres

  1. The lidar's ground-classified returns (class 2) were interpolated to a 0.5 m bare-earth surface. Under buildings and dense vegetation the ground is interpolated from the nearest ground returns.

  • Tiles fetched from the hosted layer are byte for byte the package's, and the tile counts per level equal the package's.

  • Ground as it was in October and November 2023; grading since then is not reflected.
  • Under buildings the ground is interpolated, so building sites are smoothed.
